# Kustomize CLI
`kustomize` is a command line tool exposed as an extension CLI to `gh`.

This tool utilizes [Kustomize](https://kustomize.io/) to generate kubernetes manifests from Kustomize configuration files.

For an extensive documentation on how we use Kustomize at GitHub, please refer to the [Kustomize page on The Hub](https://thehub.github.com/epd/engineering/products-and-services/internal/kustomize).

## Installation
Make sure you have the `gh` CLI installed. You can find the installation instructions [here](https://github.com/cli/cli).
```sh
gh extension install github/gh-kustomize
```

## Usage
```sh
gh kustomize <command> <args>
```

## Commands
### build
Build a set of Kubernetes resources using Kustomize. Run this command from your repository root directory.

`gh kustomize build <DIR>` will locate kustomize files located under `<DIR>/config/kustomize` and generate the manifests under `<DIR>/config/kubernetes`.

```sh
gh kustomize build                  # Runs on your current working directory
gh kustomize build path/to/repo     # Runs on the specified path
gh kustomize build -e production    # Runs on your production environment
gh kustomize build --output /out    # Outputs the generated manifests to /out (default: config/kubernetes)
gh kustomize build --dry            # Outputs the generated manifests to stdout
```
### validate
Validate kubernetes configuration files generated by kustomize.

`gh kustomize validate <DIR>` will locate kustomize files located under `<DIR>/config/kustomize` and check if they are consistent with the manifests under `<DIR>/config/kubernetes`.

This is the command that runs on CI to ensure that the generated manifests are up-to-date.
```sh
gh kustomize validate               # Runs on your current working directory
gh kustomize validate path/to/repo  # Runs on the specified path
gh kustomize validate -e production # Runs on your production environment
gh kustomize validate --verbose     # Outputs the diff between the generated manifests and the ones in the repository
```

The validation is performed by the `gh kustomize validate` command. It is used in CI workflows to validate the Kustomize configuration.

### diff 
* note: diff assumes that the changes are being made on non-main branch *

`gh kustomize diff` is a useful command when doing initial migration to `gh kustomize`. 
As contents of `/config/kubernetes/` are overriden by executing kustomize and kustomize changing order of object properties, `gh kustomize diff` was envisioned as a helper method to provide easy way to check differences between previous configuration and configuration that was generated with `gh kustomize build`.

Diff executes YAML diff (dyff)[https://github.com/homeport/dyff] between current (non-main) branch and main branch configuration.

`gh kustomize diff` will run dyff for each file found under `<DIR>/config/kubernetes` against the main branch version of the same file.

```sh
gh kustomize diff                     # Runs diff for each file fond in /config/kubernetes in given git repo
gh kustomize diff -e <environment>    # Runs on specific environment, ie. production or default
gh kustomize diff -f path/to/repo     # Runs on the individual file
```



## CI Integrations

### Moda applications linter (recommended)

A CI validation step is available out-of-the-box for **every Moda application**. It is integrated into the [Moda linter](https://github.com/github/kubernetes-config-validation), and runs as part of your CI process.

It is automatically triggered when you push changes to your repository, and runs upon detection of kustomize configs in your branch.

#### Disabling the kustomize validation step

To disable this step in the Moda linter, simply add the following line to your `config/moda/build_options.yaml` file:
```yaml
ignore_kustomize: true
```
### Auto commit (optional)

You can opt in to let `moda-config-bundle` CI job to automatically run `gh kustomize build` command and commit the generated manifests to your branch. 

This can be done by setting the `enable_kustomize_auto_commit` environment variable to `true` in the `config/moda/build_options.yaml` file.

 Note: If you already have a `config/moda/moda_test_ignore_list.yaml` file, you can rename it to `build_options.yaml` and add this line to it.
```yaml
enable_kustomize_auto_commit: true
```
